title: Build a Trust-Safe Citation Verifier
summary: Build a bounded, governed system that catches malformed, unidentified, mis-stated, and unsupported citations before they ship. All nine modules and eighteen lessons are public; enrollment, saved progress, submissions, grading, credentials, and the planned tutor are not yet available.
audience: Researchers, writers, legal teams, educators, and publishers responsible for claims that must be traceable and correct.

records.title: Define what verified means
records.summary: Separate citation form, source existence, current status, quotation accuracy, and proposition support before choosing technology.

records.title: Design the bounded workspace
records.summary: Choose the data boundary, authority hierarchy, record structure, and human roles that govern the build.

records.title: Extract citations and propositions
records.summary: Turn a document into review units without pretending that pattern matching understands the legal proposition.

records.title: Retrieve and identify the authority
records.summary: Resolve a citation against an approved source and preserve the exact result a reviewer inspected.

records.title: Test proposition support
records.summary: Compare the proposition with the retrieved passage and distinguish direct support, qualified support, conflict, silence, and ambiguity.

records.title: Issue bounded verdicts
records.summary: Make every verdict inspectable, reversible, and no stronger than the evidence.

records.title: Build the human gate
records.summary: Place named review, confidentiality, escalation, and release controls around the verifier.

records.title: Evaluate failure, not fluency
records.summary: Test against representative errors, measure false assurance, and document coverage instead of advertising an unbounded accuracy rate.

records.title: Package the verifier and its evidence
records.summary: Produce a bounded implementation, evaluation report, audit record, and deployment decision.

records.title: The five different citation failures
content: A citation can be malformed, point to no source, identify the wrong source, quote inaccurately, or fail to support the proposition. Those are different questions and require different evidence.

A structural parser can reject an impossible reporter series. It cannot establish that a well-formed citation exists, remains good law, or supports the sentence. Write those boundaries before writing code.
records.practice: Classify ten supplied examples by failure layer and write what additional evidence would be needed to resolve each one.

records.title: The verification contract
content: Define accepted inputs, covered citation families, approved sources, possible verdicts, evidence returned, abstention rules, and the person authorized to release work.
The contract must say what a pass means. If only existence was checked, the result must not imply proposition support or current precedential status.
records.practice: Complete a one-page contract with an explicit non-goal for every promised capability.

records.title: Choose the data path before the model
content: Map the document from input through parsing, retrieval, model processing, human review, export, logs, and deletion. Identify every external service and every place confidential material could persist.
Use synthetic or public material until authority, contract, account settings, retention, and supervision are resolved.
records.practice: Draw a data-flow record for a browser-local build and a connected firm build; mark every boundary where information leaves the device.

records.title: Create the review-unit schema
content: A useful review unit stores document ID, claim text, citation string, normalized citation, source snapshot, located passage, verdict, confidence, limitations, reviewer, timestamps, and version.
Keep machine output separate from human disposition. Never overwrite the evidence that produced an earlier result.
records.practice: Create one known-good and one known-bad review record and confirm that another reviewer could reproduce the disposition.

records.title: Build a transparent citation parser
content: Start with a narrow citation family and deterministic patterns. Return the matched text and parsed fields so a learner can see exactly what the parser recognized.
Unknown formats should become unparsed review items, not disappear. Measure extraction recall on the document types you actually expect.
records.practice: Run the public Citation Verifier against the sample, then add five boundary cases and record misses without changing the test labels.

records.title: Bind each citation to the proposition
content: A citation is usually attached to a sentence, clause, quotation, or string of propositions. Capture enough context for review while preserving the exact proposition being tested.
When one sentence contains multiple claims or citations, split the review units or mark the mapping ambiguous. Do not let proximity silently become support.
records.practice: Annotate a paragraph containing three claims and two citations; explain every claim-to-citation boundary.

records.title: Rank sources by authority and purpose
content: Use official court or government material when the task requires an authoritative rule or filing. Research databases and aggregators may be useful for discovery but have different coverage, licensing, status, and citator boundaries.
Record which source answered which question. A source that establishes existence may not establish current validity.
records.practice: Create an approved-source hierarchy for one jurisdiction and define the fallback when the preferred source is unavailable.

records.title: Retrieve, normalize, and preserve
content: Normalize the query, preserve the original citation, log the source and retrieval time, and return zero, one, or multiple candidates without forcing a match.
Store a permitted snapshot or stable reference to the reviewed material. Respect authentication, rate limits, licensing, and redistribution restrictions.
records.practice: Design the response for no match, one match, and ambiguous matches; require a human choice whenever identity is uncertain.

records.title: Locate the supporting passage
content: Retrieve candidate passages around meaningful terms, quotations, headings, and citations. Preserve page or paragraph locators where the source provides them.
Retrieval is a candidate-generation step. The best-scoring passage is not proof that the proposition is supported.
records.practice: For three propositions, return the strongest candidate passage and one plausible distractor; explain why ranking alone cannot issue the verdict.

records.title: Compare claim, qualification, and conflict
content: Test who, what, when, jurisdiction, conditions, degree, and exceptions. A source may support a narrower proposition while the draft overstates it.
Require the system to quote the passage, identify the mismatch, and abstain when context is incomplete. A model explanation without inspectable source text is not a verification result.
records.practice: Rewrite three overstated claims to the strongest formulation their sources actually support.

records.title: Use a verdict taxonomy that cannot hide uncertainty
content: Use bounded labels such as structurally invalid, no source located, identity ambiguous, supported, supported with qualification, contradicted, unsupported, and not verified.
Confidence describes the basis for a provisional result; it does not convert missing evidence into support.
records.practice: Assign verdicts to twelve cases and write the permitted next action for each label.

records.title: Produce an inspectable review report
content: A reviewer needs the proposition, original citation, normalized record, source link, passage, verdict, reason, unresolved issue, reviewer status, and version in one place.
Separate machine suggestion, reviewer decision, and release decision. Make changes traceable.
records.practice: Create a one-page report that lets a supervisor disagree with the result without rerunning the system.

records.title: Keep professional responsibility with the professional
content: ABA Formal Opinion 512 applies existing competence, confidentiality, communication, supervision, candor, and fee duties to lawyers using generative AI. Rule 11 separately governs representations made by presenting a paper in federal civil litigation.
The verifier assists inquiry. It does not become the lawyer, editor, researcher, or accountable releaser.
records.practice: Identify the named approver, prohibited inputs, escalation triggers, and release evidence for a high-stakes filing workflow.

records.title: Design the audit and change record
content: Record the document hash or version, tool version, ruleset, sources checked, timestamps, results, overrides, reviewer, and release status.
Log enough to reconstruct the decision without retaining confidential content longer than the approved policy permits.
records.practice: Draft an audit record and retention rule that distinguish evidentiary need from indiscriminate storage.

records.title: Build the failure-focused test set
content: Construct representative cases for valid citations, malformed forms, nonexistent authorities, wrong metadata, inaccurate quotations, overstatement, contradiction, ambiguous mapping, unavailable sources, and unsupported formats.
Keep test labels independent of the system being tested and document the coverage boundary.
records.practice: Create at least twenty labeled cases, including cases designed to expose false passes.

records.title: Measure dangerous errors
content: Report results by failure class. False passes are especially consequential because they create unwarranted assurance; false flags create review burden and may also hide systematic gaps.
Do not publish a single accuracy number without the dataset, denominator, labels, version, coverage, and error distribution.
records.practice: Calculate the confusion matrix for each verdict family and write the release decision those results justify.

records.title: Choose prototype, pilot, or deployment
content: A local demonstration, connected research pilot, governed workflow, and institutional system have different evidence, security, integration, and operational requirements.
Release only the capability level that was actually tested. Document exclusions and the conditions required to move to the next level.
records.practice: Write a deployment decision memo with a precise status label, permitted users, permitted data, known limitations, and rollback trigger.

records.title: Defend the system without overselling it
content: Present the verifier through its contract, architecture, evidence, test results, limitations, human gate, and change plan. Demonstrate one success and one abstention.
A credible defense explains what the system cannot establish and shows how the workflow responds when evidence is missing.
records.practice: Record a ten-minute capstone defense and answer the rubric questions using only evidence in the project package.

records.title: Diagnostic: distinguish the verification layers
records.passingRule: Diagnostic only; record the baseline and revisit it after Module 6.

records.title: Knowledge check: contract and verdict boundaries
records.passingRule: Earn at least 80 percent and correct every answer that would permit an unsupported pass.

questions.prompt: A citation matches a recognized reporter pattern. What has the system established?
options: The cited case exists and remains good law
Only that the text matches the implemented structural pattern
The cited source supports the proposition
questions.explanation: Structural parsing does not establish existence, current validity, or proposition support.

questions.prompt: An approved source returns no match. Which verdict is defensible?
options: No source located through the checked coverage
questions.explanation: A failed search must preserve the coverage boundary; it cannot prove fabrication by itself.

questions.prompt: The source supports a narrower claim than the draft states. What should the verifier return?
options: Supported with qualification and the mismatch identified
questions.explanation: The verdict must preserve the condition or limitation the draft omitted.

questions.prompt: Who owns the final release decision for a consequential filing?
options: The model that generated the best passage match
questions.explanation: The system assists review; accountable professional judgment and release authority stay with the authorized human.

questions.prompt: What must accompany a published accuracy number?
options: Dataset, denominator, labels, version, coverage, and error distribution
A statement that the tool is a beta
questions.explanation: A single score without its test basis hides the failures that matter.

records.title: Lab: retrieval and proposition evidence
records.passingRule: Earn at least 80 percent with a source, passage, locator, and bounded reason for every resolved review unit.

records.title: Scenario: confidential filing under time pressure
records.passingRule: Identify all prohibited transfers and require a named authorized reviewer before release.

records.title: Capstone: build and defend the verifier
records.passingRule: Earn at least 80 of 100 overall, earn at least half of every criterion, and receive no automatic-fail finding.

editorialSections.title: A fake citation is no longer a small mistake

blocks.text: Courts have sanctioned lawyers for filings containing fabricated and mis-stated authorities. "It sounded right" is not a verification method. For anyone who publishes sourced claims — lawyers, clerks, researchers, journalists, and policy writers — an unverified citation creates professional risk.

The problem is not just whether a source exists. It is whether the source actually supports the specific proposition it is cited for. That is the gap this course teaches you to close, with a tool you build and control.

editorialSections.title: A verifier that checks the claim, not just the link

blocks.text: The public course teaches you to build or specify a bounded system that takes a document and its citations and returns a per-citation review record with evidence. A working deployment depends on the learner's implementation, approved sources, testing, and human-review environment.
Every citation and its claim
Pulls each citation and the exact proposition it is cited for.
Exists and supports
Confirms the source is real and retrievable, then whether it actually supports the claim.
Fabricated, mis-stated, unsupported
A verdict per citation with the supporting passage or the gap.
A shareable audit
Verdicts, evidence, and confidence, ready to hand to a supervisor.
An audit trail
Every check recorded, so it is provable and not merely asserted.
Human signs off
On doubt it defaults to flag for review. You stay accountable; the tool assists.

editorialSections.title: A claim you can't back up is a bill waiting to arrive

blocks.text: Regulators are active right now. The FTC opens cases over unsubstantiated health, performance, and green claims; the FDA sends warning letters over disease and structure-function language; state AGs and platforms pull listings and ads that overstate. A single line of copy that promises more than your evidence supports can trigger a penalty, a warning letter, or a takedown.

The hard part is not knowing rules exist. It is catching the specific claim, mapping it to the specific rule, and knowing what proof it needs, before the copy goes live. That is the gap this course teaches you to close, with a tool you build and own.

editorialSections.title: A checker that reads your copy the way a regulator would

blocks.text: By the end you have a working system that takes a piece of copy, an ad, a label, a product page, an email, and returns a per-claim verdict with the rule behind it and the substantiation it requires.
Every claim in the copy
Pulls each express and implied claim, not just the obvious headline.
Claim to the rule
Matches each claim to the applicable regime: FTC substantiation, FDA, state, industry code.
Unsubstantiated, overstated, prohibited
A verdict per claim with the reason and the risk level.
The substantiation needed
Tells you what proof each claim needs before it can run, or that it cannot run at all.
A review-ready audit
Verdicts, rules, and required proof, ready to hand to legal or a client.
Human signs off
On doubt it defaults to flag for review. You stay accountable; the tool assists.

editorialSections.title: The gap is not knowledge. It is permission to begin.

blocks.text: You have watched people build with AI and felt behind. The block is rarely the concepts — it is not knowing where to start, and fear of doing it wrong. This course removes both. You pick one workflow, build a small team around it, and finish the weekend with a working system and your own hands on the controls.
It is deliberately small. That is the point. A tiny team you actually understand beats a sprawling one you cannot govern. When you outgrow it, the deeper courses are waiting.

editorialSections.title: A small team with a job and a boundary each

blocks.text: By the end you have a supervised team of five or six named agents running one real workflow — and stopping at you before anything goes out.
One real workflow
Trigger, inputs, steps, decisions, output — written as a chain a coworker could follow.
What AI should and shouldn't do
Sort each step into off-limits, augmentation, or automation. The safe default is augmentation.
A named team
Chief of Staff, Researcher, Drafter, Reviewer, Compliance, Ops — the ones your workflow needs.
A role contract per agent
May do X, may never do Y, must route Z to you. The line that makes it real.
A human-approval step
The team works up to "ready to send" — then stops for your sign-off. Every time.
One clean end-to-end pass
Run the team on a real task, watch what breaks, tighten, and run it again.

editorialSections.title: A named team is cute. The contract under the name is the product.

blocks.text: Anyone can give agents fun names. What makes a team usable — for a founder, a clinic, a law practice — is the contract under each name: what it may touch, what it may never do, and what it must route to you.
May flag or block off-brand output · may never send · must route publish decisions to you.
May check claims and risk · may never approve its own work · must escalate any risk to you.
May prepare the finished work · may never publish alone · every send is approval-gated.

editorialSections.title: A weekend, in four build-blocks

blocks.text: You do not watch and forget. You leave each block with a working piece of your team.

items: See your work as a system. Pick one workflow and map it — trigger, inputs, steps, decisions, output, accountability. Clarity before agents.

editorialSections.title: The Approval Gate is the product

blocks.text: You will build the wall that makes an agent trustworthy: it plans and prepares freely, but any send, post, DM, spend, or change-settings action is default-denied until you approve the exact payload.
perceive → plan → select tool → ⏺ approval gate → execute → verify → log
Edit the action and the prior approval is void. No unauthorized action, provable and not promised.

editorialSections.title: An agent that acts on its own is a liability, not an asset

blocks.text: Everyone is selling AI that runs while you sleep. For real work, client emails, posts, payments, settings, an agent that acts unsupervised is one bad call away from sending the wrong thing to the wrong person. In law, healthcare-adjacent, and client work, that is not a bug. It is a breach.
The fix is not less capability. It is a hard wall: the agent does everything reversible on its own, and stops for your approval before anything consequential.

editorialSections.title: An operator you own that can't go rogue

blocks.text: By the end you have a supervised operator that acts across your tools, sounds like you, and structurally cannot take a consequential action without your sign-off.
Across your tools
Research, drafting, file and inbox prep across the apps you connect.
Your voice
Drafts in your writing style via your own corpus, retrieval not fine-tuning, so it stays deletable.
At the gate
Consequential actions wait for your explicit approval. Enforced structurally, not as a setting.
With permission
Context in retrieval you can inspect and delete, not baked into a model.
Against injection
Treats everything it reads from web and email as data, not instructions.
Everything
An append-only audit trail. No unauthorized action is provable.

editorialSections.title: A confidently wrong assistant is worse than no assistant

blocks.text: Everyone is rushing to point an AI assistant at their existing docs. But if the knowledge base is stale, contradictory, full of gaps, or salted with sensitive data, the assistant will answer wrong with total confidence, and cite your own documents while doing it. It will also happily surface the salary sheet or the unredacted contract to whoever asks.

You cannot govern an assistant into being right if the source is broken. The fix is to assess and prepare the knowledge base first, for coverage, freshness, structure, contradictions, and sensitive data, before anything reads from it. That is what this course teaches you to build.

editorialSections.title: A checker that grades the source before the assistant reads it

blocks.text: By the end you have a working tool that takes a knowledge base and returns a readiness report of what is missing, stale, contradictory, and sensitive, plus a prepared version ready for retrieval.
Coverage and gaps
Finds the questions your knowledge base cannot answer before your users do.
Freshness
Flags documents too old to trust and the ones overdue for review.
Structure
Rates how retrievable the content is: chunkable, labeled, findable.
Contradictions
Surfaces documents that disagree, so the assistant does not pick one at random.
Sensitive data
Flags PII, secrets, and confidential material that should not be retrievable.
Human signs off

editorialSections.title: Regulation moves faster than any inbox can keep up with

blocks.text: Fifty states plus federal agencies are all moving at once. A bill you did not see gets introduced, amended, and enrolled while you are watching a different one. For a regulated operator, missing a single change can mean a blown compliance deadline, a lost lobbying window, or advice that is already out of date.

Manual tracking does not scale and news alerts summarize badly. What you need is a tool that watches the primary sources, scores relevance to your organization, and summarizes each change with a citation you can verify. Build it once and you stop guessing.

Rates each item against your organization's profile so noise drops away.
What actually changed

The primary source
Every summary links back to the bill or rule text, verifiable and not paraphrased into thin air.
What matters, to whom
Routes high-relevance changes to the right person with a clear reason.
Human signs off

editorialSections.title: Most AI adoption fails quietly, and no one can say why

blocks.text: Businesses are spending on AI tools with unclear ROI and no plan. Pilots stall, teams pick the flashy use case over the valuable one, and the risky workflow gets automated first. When leadership asks whether it worked, nobody has an answer they can defend.

What is missing is a rigorous audit: a repeatable way to map the real workflows, score which ones are ready, flag which ones are risky, and rank what to do first. Build that audit once and you own a method you can sell to every business that is guessing.

A defensible roadmap

Evidence, not opinion
